title: Large Discrete Policy: Advancing Explicit Behavior Modeling with Stochastic Iterative Scoring
claim: Existing paradigms trade off expressivity against plausibility and interpretability; ours combines iterative stochastic refinement with an explicit discrete candidate set.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, per-panel ✓/✗ checklists, ours highlighted in blue
description: Three side-by-side panels compare behavior-modeling paradigms. Each panel is a vertical flow diagram. Panel (a), Iterative Denoising Policy, starts with a noise point cloud. Condition image icons feed yellow Action Decoder boxes, and a dotted arrow marks repeated denoising. It ends in a noisy and a clean green action curve. Panel (b), One-shot Discrete Policy, starts with a fixed vocabulary of blue trajectories. A single decoder scores them (0.1, 0.3, 0.6) and selects one action. Panel (c), Ours, has a light-blue background and green decoder boxes. It repeats the decoder with stochastic scoring over the fixed vocabulary, then selects an action. Each panel ends with a checklist, using green ticks for strengths and red crosses for weaknesses. Panel (c) has only ticks. The eye goes first to the blue-highlighted panel (c) and the checklists.
caption: Paradigms for Behavior Modeling Policies. (a) Iterative denoising policies generate actions through stochastic iterative refinement, offering strong expressivity but remaining an implicit and less interpretable generation process. (b) One-shot discrete policies explicitly select from a fixed action vocabulary, but are limited by single-pass scoring. (c) Our approach combines the strengths of both paradigms by performing stochastic iterative scoring over a discrete action vocabulary, enabling expressive, plausible, and interpretable behavior generation.
abstract: Behavior policies are often formulated as continuous generative models, whose iterative denoising processes are expressive but difficult to interpret and prone to producing implausible actions. We propose the Large Discrete Policy (LDiP), a fully discrete behavior modeling framework that selects actions from a large vocabulary of physically plausible candidates. Rather than perturbing actions, LDiP improves expressivity through stochastic iterative scoring: it progressively re-scores and prunes candidates with score-space stochasticity, enabling fine-grained ranking and exploration among plausible actions while preserving an explicit decision process. Across end-to-end planning, closed-loop driving, robotic manipulation, and vision-language-action settings, LDiP consistently outperforms strong discrete and continuous baselines in autonomous driving, and exceeds or matches continuous generative policies in robotic manipulation. These results show that discrete policies, when equipped with effective scoring mechanisms, offer an expressive, plausible, and interpretable alternative for behavior modeling. Project website: https://zhenxinli.net/LargeDiscretePolicy/.
